chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not make me like the water container of the rider, for the rider fills his container and drinks it whenever he desires. Make me [part of] the beginning of the supplication, and at its end, and in its middle.'
ai.seo_question: Why should blessings upon the Prophet be included throughout the supplication?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s instruction to integrate salawat continuously throughout supplication, ensuring his spiritual presence remains central rather than peripheral. In Shia tradition, this emphasizes the enduring intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt and the necessity of maintaining a constant connection with the Prophet during du'a, reflecting the concept of 'tawassul' through his household.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not make me<sup>saww</sup> to be like the water container of the rider, so the rider fills his water container and he drinks it whenever he so desires to. Make me<sup>saww</sup> to be at the beginning of the supplication and at the end of it, and in the middle of it’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Do not consider me as the water container of a traveler who fills up his water container and drinks from it whenever he wants. You should place me at the beginning of your prayer, at the end of it and in the middle.’”
